sections.overview: This small, metallic blue-black carpenter bee occurs across much of Europe and is a solitary stem-nesting bee, unlike the much larger wood-boring Xylocopa carpenter bees.
sections.identification: It is only about 7–9 mm long; the male usually has a pale clypeus while the female’s is dark, and its compact metallic body separates it from larger Xylocopa.
sections.habitat: It frequents sunny flower-rich places where dead pithy stems remain available for nesting, including bramble, mullein and other hollow or soft-centred plants.
sections.diet: The females collect pollen from many plant families rather than relying on one host flower, and adults also take nectar.
sections.behavior: Females excavate a linear nest tunnel in a pithy stem; adults overwinter in stems, and the species is usually solitary, although social nesting occurs in some other Ceratina.
sections.reproduction: After mating in spring, a female provisions a row of brood cells with pollen and nectar for the developing larvae; the species normally has one generation per year.
sections.ecology: It is a close European congener of C. cucurbitina: German bee specialists note that C. cyanea appears earlier and is metallic, whereas C. cucurbitina lacks that metallic sheen.
sections.conservation: The European Red List assesses it as Least Concern; retaining dead hollow stems in sunny sites nevertheless supports its nesting opportunities.
